answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to stake a small, time-locked deposit backed by verifiable work history, like rings in timber that prove slow growth. Reputation then compounds only through attested, useful actions, so creating many fake agents is costly and slow. Like a walnut shell, the stake protects the kernel of trust, while cheap mass identities spiral into unprofitability because each fake must pay the same price as a real one.
